article_title: Chrome 154 Ships Content-Sized Iframes, Accessible Scroll-Marker Modes and text-decoration-inset

content_preview.title: Chrome 154 Ships Content-Sized Iframes, Accessible Scroll-Marker Modes and text-decoration-inset
content_preview.summary: Chrome 154 reached stable on September 22 with a frame-sizing property for iframes that size to their content, links and tabs modes for scroll markers, and text-decoration-inset.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Chrome 154 is the browser's newest stable release, with a stable release date of September 22, 2026, according to the [Chrome 154 release notes](https://developer.chrome.com/release-notes/154). Google's [New in Chrome 154](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/new-in-chrome-154) post highlights three web-platform features: responsively-sized iframes, new modes for the CSS `scroll-marker-group` property, and a `text-decoration-inset` property. The release notes also list a default prompt...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well structured News piece (731 words, within 400-1200). Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know, Context. Technical detail is accurate and appropriately scoped.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three gzipped snapshots from disk (source-0.html.gz = developer.chrome.com/blog/new-in-chrome-154, source-1.html.gz = developer.chrome.com/blog/responsive-iframes, source-2.html.gz = developer.chrome.com/release-notes/154); all HTTP 200, no archive fallback. Verified verbatim: (1) source-0: 'letting an <iframe> element in a parent document size itself to the embedded document's layout overflow sizing so that scrolling in the child document is avoided'; the postMessage() replacement pattern; frame-sizing: content-height on the embedding page; '<meta name="responsive-embedded-sizing"> element in its <head>'; scroll-marker-group links (default) and tabs modes setting focus order and WAI-ARIA semantics; text-decoration-inset accepting auto, length and percentage in one- or two-value syntax, positive values inset (shorter), negative outset (longer), animated underline reveal instead of background gradients or extra elements. (2) source-1: supported values auto/content-width/content-height/content-inline-size/content-block-size; meta tag cannot be added dynamically after load; browser does not continuously observe layout changes; window.requestResize(); 'best to call window.requestResize() before layout, after all changes to the document have been made'; explicit update model avoids resize loops; allow-origins=https://publisher.example with space-separated multiple origins; complements CSP frame-ancestors; @supports (frame-sizing: content-height) fallback; Core Web Vitals content-shift caveat for first viewport. (3) source-2: stable release date September 22nd, 2026; links mode as navigation list with link-role markers all sequential tab stops; tabs mode tablist/tab/tabpanel, only active marker is a tab stop, arrow-key navigation; Ask before HTTP on by default with HttpsOnlyMode policy; WebSocket options dictionary and targetAddressSpace conditional on local network permission and local IP resolution; CSSStyleValue exposed to Workers; font-width alias for font-stretch; Iterator.prototype.includes(). Every claim confirmed. developer.chrome.com is on config/source_allowlist.txt (line 136). Manifest suspicious_patterns null for all three sources; nothing to check.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinations, misattributions or unsourced specifics. Headline, summary and lead each backed by the cited sources. Minor note: the summary's 'reached stable on September 22' matches the release notes and blog post date. Body attributes each claim to the correct one of the three sources; no orphan URLs (only the internal Safari 27 link, which is not a source).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, attributed to the Chrome team throughout; no editorializing or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior article on Chrome 154 or these CSS/iframe features (grepped articles for frame-sizing, text-decoration-inset, scroll-marker, Chrome 154). Only related prior coverage is the Aug 2026 Chrome/Edge/Firefox release-cycle article and the Safari 27 release article.
editor_notes.cross_reference_check: The Safari 27 internal link /article/2026-09/25-safari-27-ships-with-safari-mcp-for-ai-coding-agents-customizable-select-styling-and-a-rewritten-ecmascript-module-loader resolves to an existing published article at src/content/articles/2026-09/25-safari-27-ships-...-module-loader.md and is correctly in singular /article/ form. The article's 'What We Don't Know' hedge (cited Chrome docs do not state when other engines will support frame-sizing or text-decoration-inset; no adoption figures) is not contradicted by any of the three sources: none mention other-engine plans, and the Chrome 154 snapshots contain no such statements. The responsive-iframes snapshot's 'Browser Support' widget is empty in the snapshot and does not contradict the hedge.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurate, well-sourced developer-news article. All feature claims verified verbatim against the three developer.chrome.com snapshots. APPROVE.
